executiveSummary: GM0373 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, headline demography, 36 neighbourhoods, seven BAG places, 16 BRT settlements, five NWB links, null semantics, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, exact zero-intensity behavior and event-attributable service person-hours are coherent. Release nevertheless remains correction-required for three reproducible spatial-evidence defects. The coastal preset derives municipality-wide stress solely from centroid distance to a three-segment coastline: at T+24 its internal inundation-stress amplitude is 2.290157, system pressure 0.573105 and modeled population under pressure 18,136, although no failed dune/defence, water level, return period, connected flood footprint, arrival or recession scenario is selected. This does not mean Bergen lacks coastal risk; the municipality says current safety is in order while HHNK is actively managing future weak points, so the simulator must identify the hypothetical failure and source layer before presenting local impacts. Coastal and pluvial maps have the identical exact 36-neighbourhood order, proving they are a shared seeded allocation rather than mechanism-specific geography. A focused synthetic wildfire placed inside BU03730700 Schoorl met Bregtdorp ranks that containing neighbourhood only 13th, while BU03730401 Prins Hendrik Stichting, about 9.271 km from the source, ranks first. Official local evidence makes coast/dunes, Schoorlse Duinen fire access and extinguishing water, Egmondermeer/Sammerspolder rainwater response, and PWN's dune-based drinking-water chain material. Public water objects and provider areas are valuable context but do not currently alter simulation. All eight utility views honestly call their reused N9/N504/N512 flows logical transfer proxies. Physical PWN, Liander, sewer, telecom, facility and emergency-supply topology, live state, backup, stocks, crews and restoration estimates remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2022–2023, extended through 2024
evidenceSources.edition: adopted 2022-03-04; later regional policy identifies it as extended through 2024
supports: The region distinguishes North Sea/Wadden/IJsselmeer-Markermeer flooding, a primary-water-defence or polder-dike breach and shorter cluster-rain consequences; it does not support one unnamed municipality-wide coastal depth.

Coastal nature areas are sensitive to major forest and dune fire, drought raises risk, nearby villages/recreation include vulnerable objects, and firefighting and evacuation can be difficult and time-consuming.
The profile specifically cites Bergen/Schoorl dune fires in 2009–2011 and measures including a nature-fire plan, drones, specialist vehicles, water wells and land-manager cooperation.

Long electricity outage, ICT/digital disruption and cyber cascading effects are material; drinking water, gas, wastewater and food disruption are retained as vital-process context even when not separately selected as profile scenarios.
Small historical earthquakes between Alkmaar and Bergen reached magnitude 3.2, but the profile assesses probability and physical effects as very small.

This is a static expert-judgement profile, not a live feed or local probability/depth surface. Its stated period is expired and no machine API, fixed refresh cadence or explicit redistribution licence is provided; current use is contextual only.

supports: The municipality reports water safety along its entire coast is currently in order and that dunes are growing with sea-level rise; this is current defence context, not a claim that a hypothetical breach cannot occur.
HHNK's Veerkrachtige Kust calculations identify possible future weak points and actions including raising beach accesses, opening/closing notches and raising low rear-boundary locations.
Egmond aan Zee and Bergen aan Zee require place- and cross-section-specific interpretation; targeted sand nourishment and dynamic coast management are part of the actual system.

The newsletter is a dated authoritative PDF without a fixed machine update cadence or explicit reuse licence. HHNK's public ArcGIS Veerkrachtige Kust viewer exposes queryable scenario/context layers, but its item declares no licence and is not a breach-inundation forecast.

evidenceSources.title: Extreme neerslag — June 2021 evaluation context
supports: More than 100 mm and locally 140 mm fell within 24 hours, followed a day later by 40–60 mm; the most acute water nuisance included Sammerspolder and Egmondermeer inside GM0373.
Watercourses reached ground level and water remained on land; response took time and prompted criticism of response speed and water-system capacity.

This is authoritative observed historical/event-evaluation context, not a live feed, design return period or reusable hydraulic raster. The page has no fixed update cadence, machine API or explicit data licence.

evidenceSources.title: Van oppervlaktewater naar drinkwater in Bergen
supports: Bergen drinking-water production depends on IJsselmeer/Lek intake and pretreatment, transfer through Heemskerk, dune infiltration between Bergen and Wijk aan Zee for at least several weeks, final treatment in Bergen and blending with purified Jan Lagrand water from Heemskerk.
The Bergen production facility borders the dune area, establishing a material local water/nature dependency without disclosing sensitive network topology.

This is authoritative current process/context, not a licensed machine topology, pressure zone, telemetry, outage, backup or restoration API; no fixed page-update cadence or explicit reuse licence is stated.

findings.summary: A coarse coast-distance field presents unsupported municipality-wide direct inundation without a selected Bergen defence-failure scenario.
findings.evidence: E03 distinguishes North Sea flooding and a primary-defence/polder breach; E04 says current Bergen coast safety is in order while identifying future weak points and location-specific measures. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:464-480 nevertheless uses only centroid distance to three coarse coast segments, and lines 644-650 turn that screen into direct local stress. At T+6/T+12/T+24 the canonical coastal preset emits the same internal inundation-stress amplitude 2.290157 and derived-screening spatial evidence. It produces 19,456 modeled people/47,031 event-attributable service person-hours at T+6, 18,136/338,129 at T+24 and, after forcing clears, 7,857/1,063,455 at T+72. No failed dune/defence, section, present condition, surge/water level, probability, connected footprint, arrival or recession supports the magnitude. This is municipality-specific evidence of the shared national coastal-screen defect, not a claim that Bergen lacks coastal risk or that official current safety guarantees future safety.
findings.action: Mark GM0373's current direct coastal result unsupported/Unknown for operational decisions until an expert selects a named/versioned defence-failure scenario. Preserve current defence context and hypothetical coast risk separately. The durable fix must intersect approved LIWO depth/arrival/duration and HHNK defence/cross-section layers, retain scenario ID, failed element, present/future defence state, units, probability class, version, no-data, licence and uncertainty, and expose only connected affected population/services.

findings.evidence: The mandatory harness passes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services; zero-intensity output is exact zero; the direct-zero named-river event accumulates zero event-attributable service person-hours despite non-unit baseline service values; local compound T+24 population/affected/service balances reconcile; ledgers close; all eleven layer selections preserve simulation state; and every route says logical-proxy.
findings.action: Retain these assertions as regression gates while adding authoritative spatial adapters; do not weaken deterministic, reconciliation or exact-zero behavior to hide calibration gaps.

corrections.summary: Stop exposing Bergen's coast-distance scalar as supported local inundation and require a selected current/forecast defence-failure scenario.
corrections.validation: Interim: set GM0373 coastal direct spatialEvidence to unsupported, expose local direct water/affected/service consequences as Unknown or numerically neutral for operational use, and retain wind plus current defence context separately; do not describe this as no risk. Re-run pnpm test plus focused and ALL municipality gates. Durable machine source: LIWO GeoServer OWS https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows and catalogue API https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2 provide named/versioned depth, arrival and duration scenario products. LIWO is release/layer-versioned rather than fixed-cadence and its portal provides no blanket redistribution licence, so retain scenario/layer/version/retrieval and clear terms before caching. HHNK's public Veerkrachtige Kust ArcGIS layer https://kaarten.hhnk.nl/arcgis/rest/services/veerkrachtige_kust/Veerkrachtige_kust/MapServer/0 exposes queryable cross-section/SLR context (public web-map item modified 2026-04-21), but licenseInfo is blank and there is no promised cadence; it may qualify defence/future-state context, never substitute for a breach footprint. Keringen IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-keringen-imwa/ogc/v1 is CC BY-SA 4.0 national defence geometry, not defence performance.

corrections.summary: Replace shared Bergen coast/pluvial neighbourhood seeds with source-specific scenario grids and hydraulically relevant context.
corrections.validation: Preferred local source is an HHNK/municipality licensed native stress-test or hydraulic export for Sammerspolder, Egmondermeer and coastal compartments, with event/return period, cell size, units, edition, no-data, uncertainty, licence and retrieval retained. National fallback: Klimaateffectatlas downloads/WMS documented at https://www.klimaateffectatlas.nl/en/faq provide map-specific GeoTIFF/GeoPackage/WMS products under CC BY 4.0 and are updated several times per year; they are indicative and not a local decision model. AHN WCS https://service.pdok.nl/rws/actueel-hoogtebestand-nederland/wcs/v1_0?SERVICE=WCS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities provides 0.5 m DTM/DSM, cyclical editions and CC0 terrain. E08 IMWA/DAMO and GWSW OGC https://api.pdok.nl/rioned/waterschappen-waterketen-gwsw/ogc/v1 provide partial official context only. Tests must preserve Unknown no-data, permit coast/pluvial rankings to differ and prove approved source cells govern local direct impact.

corrections.summary: Make explicit Bergen/Schoorl wildfire scenarios source-, fuel- and weather-aware while keeping response resources Unknown unless authorized.
corrections.validation: Preferred source is NIPV's Risiko-index Natuurbranden at https://nipv.nl/informatievoorziening/voorzieningen/risico-index-natuurbranden/, a professional 1 km² product. No public documented bulk API, redistribution licence or fixed cadence is available, so request an authorized export/terms. Public fallback: Kadaster BRT TOP10NL OGC https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-top10nl/ogc/v1 provides national 1:10,000 land cover/topography under CC BY 4.0 with editioned releases, combined with timestamped KNMI Open Data weather whose product-specific licence/validity is retained. Static cover is not live fuel moisture or spread. Tests must rank the source-intersecting neighbourhood above a distant non-intersecting one under equal conditions and expose wind, fuel, access, extinguishing-water and suppression assumptions separately.

corrections.summary: Add Bergen drainage and drinking-water dependency context without inventing operational topology, current state or restoration capacity.
corrections.validation: E08 Kunstwerken IMWA/Waterketen DAMO are machine OGC Features under CC BY-SA 4.0 and yield 349 intersecting partial objects; retain retrieval/object timestamps, contributor completeness and affectsSimulation=false. Waterbeheergebieden IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterbeheergebieden-imwa/ogc/v1 and GWSW can add drainage/level/sewer context, but connectivity/control/state must remain Unknown without licensed authority data. E07 supports named PWN process-stage nodes only; no public licensed distribution topology, telemetry, backup or restoration API was found. The provider-territory WMS at https://public.geodata.mijnaansluiting.nl/geoserver/mijnaansluiting_open/ows supplies live responsibility polygons with provider timestamps, not assets/state. Liander open electricity/gas geometry at https://www.liander.nl/over-ons/open-data is CC BY 4.0 official context with unstated fixed refresh cadence; it cannot establish loading, switching, pressure, outage or repair. Exercise effects require approved bounded fixtures and sensitivity tests.

corrections.summary: Separate static mobility context, live observations and synthetic utility transfer proxies throughout Bergen's first-72-hour graph.
corrections.validation: NWB OGC https://api.pdok.nl/rws/nationaal-wegenbestand-wegen/ogc/v1 is Rijkswaterstaat/PDOK static road geometry, monthly and CC0; it may update mobility topology, never power/water/drainage/gas/telecom capacity. NDW Open Data https://opendata.ndw.nu/ exposes timestamped DATEX II speeds, queues, incidents, closures, measures and works at feed-specific cadence; retain validity and expire stale records to Unknown. GTFS schedule validity does not prove buses operate. Add regression tests that only matching location/direction/mode/validity can alter mobility/supply and that all utility proxy labels remain explicit until service-specific authorized graphs exist.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, evacuation model, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved GM0373 LIWO/HHNK coastal breach, present defence-state, connected depth, arrival, duration or recession grid is ingested; internal inundation stress is not measured local metres.

The current official statement that Bergen's coast safety is in order must not be converted to zero future risk; equally, a generic hypothetical surge must not be presented without a failed defence/scenario.
No licensed native Bergen/HHNK pluvial raster or hydraulic model is ingested for Sammerspolder, Egmondermeer, low polders, dune seepage, sewer surcharge or receiving-water controls.

CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve buildings, elevation depressions, dune cross-sections, polders, catchments, forests, fuels, streams, sewers, households, visitors or individual vulnerability.
CBS resident population omits changing beach, campsite and nature-area visitors; no hourly visitor/occupancy feed is available and no population was invented.
The 2022–2024 regional risk profile is expired strategic expert judgement; no newer published profile was found during the bounded audit, so it cannot supply current probabilities or operations.
The public Waterschapshuis layer is intentionally partial; 349 intersecting points cannot be interpreted as a complete hydraulic/sewer system or current operational state.
Provider polygons identify responsibility at one reference point, not full physical coverage, topology or state; drainage may be missing and fixed-media areas do not represent mobile coverage.
No physical PWN, Liander, drainage, telecom, care or emergency-supply topology, live state, backup, priority customers, crew, fuel, spare or restoration estimate is available to the model.
PWN's production facility and process are public context, but precise network topology, vulnerability and operational state may be security-sensitive and were not inferred.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse NWB-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food routes.
Static NWB and GTFS inputs do not establish live closure, timetable/vehicle operation, congestion, beach/dune access, evacuation throughput or repair access; no railway station lies inside GM0373.
Facilities and supply lack verified care roles, beds, staff, acceptance, shelters, pharmacies, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, current fuel/moisture surface, wind-aware spread, suppression state and resource access; the focused Schoorl-area case is explicitly synthetic.
Earthquake lacks a selected local event, ground-motion surface, site response and asset fragility; the canonical Groningen event does not test local Bergen/Alkmaar earthquake response.
Cyber disruption is a configured exercise without operator incident telemetry, targeted-system inventory or local restoration evidence.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls rather than observed Bergen resources or commitments.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, surge arrival, dispatch and restrictions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
The ten canonical presets omit hazardous-material, pipeline, maritime/rescue, aviation and other risks present in the regional profile.

Audit all North-Holland dune municipalities with polygon/source-aware wildfire allocation and authorized NIPV RIN or transparent BRT/KNMI fallback; municipality-centroid flame screening plus neighbourhood hash is not an incident footprint.

Coordinate HHNK IMWA/DAMO/GWSW drainage objects and areas as non-causal context unless hydraulic connectivity, controls, emergency power and operational state are authorized; retain contributor completeness per municipality.
Coordinate PWN's public source/treatment/infiltration process and Liander/provider areas as responsibility/context only; do not infer sensitive topology, current availability or restoration.

Review the expired Noord-Holland-Noord risk-profile context programme-wide and pin the next adopted profile when published; static expert judgement must not be treated as a live feed or probability surface.
